stories.headline: Russia fires Oreshnik hypersonic missile at Kyiv region in one of war's largest strikes, killing four
stories.summary: Russia launched its Oreshnik intermediate-range ballistic missile for the third time against Ukraine overnight on May 23-24, as part of a mass attack involving roughly 90 missiles and 600 drones that killed four people and injured nearly 100. The missile struck Bila Tserkva in Kyiv Oblast; the Cabinet of Ministers building and the National Art Museum were among structures damaged. Zelensky warned the attack 'sets a global precedent' and called for international consequences; Foreign Minister Sybiha described it as one of the largest terrorist attacks on Kyiv and demanded an emergency UN Security Council session.

stories.headline: Ukraine's deep-strike campaign against Russian oil and industrial infrastructure escalates
stories.summary: Ukraine conducted multiple drone strikes against Russian oil refineries and energy infrastructure during the week, including the Syzran refinery (800+ km from the border), the Yaroslavl refinery (hit for the second time in a week, ~700 km away), the Metafrax Chemicals plant in Perm Krai (~1,700 km from the border, struck by SBU), and the Vtorovo fuel pumping station in Vladimir Oblast supplying the Moscow region. Zelensky described the campaign as 'long-range sanctions' on Russian energy, and Svyrydenko reported the strikes had reduced Russian oil-refining capacity by 10%.

stories.headline: Putin orders military to prepare retaliation after Russia accuses Ukraine of striking student dormitory in Starobilsk
stories.summary: Russian President Putin ordered his military to prepare retaliation options after accusing Ukraine of striking a student dormitory at Starobilsk College in Russian-occupied Luhansk, with the death toll rising to 18. Ukraine's military denied targeting civilians, saying the strike hit the headquarters of Russia's elite Rubicon drone unit. Russia convened an emergency UN Security Council session; Ukraine's ambassador rejected the accusations as propaganda.

stories.headline: Zelensky rejects Germany's associate EU membership proposal, demands full accession path
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky wrote to EU leaders calling a German Chancellor Merz proposal to grant Ukraine 'associate' EU membership without voting rights 'unfair,' arguing Ukraine deserves full rights as a country defending Europe. Foreign Minister Sybiha neither endorsed nor rejected the proposal but stressed full membership remains Ukraine's goal. The debate intensified after Hungary's Orbán, who had blocked Ukraine's bid, left office.

stories.headline: Ukraine claims tactical initiative on frontline; Syrskyi reports Russian losses exceeding 141,500 in 2026
stories.summary: Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi, in multiple public statements and a briefing at NATO headquarters in Brussels, said Ukrainian offensive actions outnumber Russian ones for the first time and that Russia has lost more than 141,500 troops since January — more than it can mobilize monthly. Zelensky confirmed Ukraine has liberated 590 square kilometers of territory in 2026 and approved long-range strike plans for June. Syrskyi also announced a troop rotation reform involving three-shift cycles every two months.

stories.headline: Lukashenko says Belarus will not enter the war; Ukraine engages Belarusian opposition as Tsikhanouskaya visit announced
stories.summary: Belarusian President Lukashenko stated Belarus will not be drawn into the war but pledged joint defense with Russia if attacked, and offered to meet Zelensky. Ukraine dismissed the offer and instead announced Foreign Minister Sybiha had met Belarusian opposition leader Tsikhanouskaya, with a Kyiv visit expected soon. Sybiha briefed NATO allies in Helsingborg on growing Belarus threats.

stories.headline: Fedorov drives drone warfare modernization: private air defense, cheap interceptors, ground robots
stories.summary: Defense Minister Fedorov briefed media on multiple defense tech initiatives: 27 companies joined Ukraine's private air defense pilot project with two already conducting combat missions; Ukraine is developing and testing low-cost interceptor missiles for Shahed drones; ground robots conducted over 21,500 missions in Q1; and Ukraine's 'ePoints' battlefield performance system is targeting 50,000 Russian casualties per month. Fedorov attributed Ukraine's improved interception rates partly to denial of Starlink to Russian forces.

stories.headline: US-brokered peace talks reach exhaustion point; Sybiha calls for European engagement
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha declared that US-facilitated talks with Russia are 'gradually reaching a point of exhaustion,' with the same issues repeatedly debated. He called for stronger European involvement to bring new momentum, stressed that no individual EU capital should seek bilateral contacts with Putin, and said Ukraine keeps the invitation open for a US delegation to visit Kyiv. Germany's conservative spokesman said any European mediator role must be decided by Zelensky.

articles.title: Kyiv Warns US-Russia Peace Track Nears Impasse as Ukraine Seeks European Push
